## Business concepts
- invoice lifecycle (aka status, queue state): An invoice moves RECEIVED -> READY -> CLAIMED -> IN_REVIEW -> CLOSED or NO_REVIEW_NEEDED; unworked invoices past the lapse window become LAPSED. Every transition is a row in invoice_history (from_status, to_status, actor, at); the invoices table stores only the current status.
- finding (aka flag, rule hit): One rule hit on an invoice (or one of its lines). rule_name is the rule that fired (rate_variance, total_mismatch, ...; compliance findings are named compliance_<rule code>); category routes it to a team (MATERIAL/SERVICE/FEE/COMPLIANCE/CORRECTION/ CREEPBACK/NOTE); amount is the dollar impact, NULL for flat flag-style findings.
- opportunity (aka recovery opportunity, dollars on the table, savings, productivity): The recovery dollars an audit of this invoice might yield — the sum of effective finding amounts plus (when larger than the service findings) the benchmark service-hours delta priced at the contract labor rate. Stored on invoices.opportunity by the roll-up.
- weight (aka priority, score): Queue priority: opportunity-derived, multiplied for creep-back (x2) and ignored corrections (x5), boosted flat for critical compliance, then divided by invoice total — density of opportunity per review hour, not raw dollars. Stored on invoices.weight.
- revision chain (aka resubmission): A resubmitted invoice arrives as a new row with the same (supplier_id, invoice_number) and revision + 1, linked by prior_revision_id. supplier_acceptance records whether the supplier ACCEPTED or REJECTED the prior review's requested changes.
- creep-back (aka creepback, creep back, raised prices back up, reinflation, price creep): A supplier accepts a corrected rate on one revision, then quietly drifts the price back up on a later one. Detected by the creepback scan; lands as CREEPBACK findings and doubles the invoice's weight multiplier.
- lapse (aka stale, expiry): Invoices still RECEIVED/READY past the lapse window (lapse_after_days, default 6, plus one fixed grace day) are swept to LAPSED by the daily stale sweep — unless protected by a critical compliance score (invoices.compliance_score >= 1500).
- network supplier: suppliers.network = 1 means in-network: their invoices enter the audit pipeline. Out-of-network suppliers' invoices are born LAPSED (out of audit scope), not scored. Those invoices carry NULL invoice_total and no invoice_lines — a total over them is NULL (no data, rendered as a dash), never $0 — and two suppliers have no invoices at all.
- audit rules (aka rules, audit rule): "Rules" has three senses. (1) The 12 audit rules in the rules engine's code — every one runs on every scored invoice, so "how many rules run on an invoice" is 12, answered from the primer/CKG, not SQL. (2) Compliance rule codes — compliance_rules rows, severity-bearing, arriving as compliance_<code> findings; 10 distinct rule codes in this data. (3) findings.rule_name values — the rules that actually FIRED (26 distinct values, since compliance findings arrive as compliance_<code>). Counting compliance_reports per invoice answers none of these.
- review report (aka corrections we request, corrections we requested, requested corrections, correction request, correction requests, audit adjustments, what we asked them to change, auditor corrections): An auditor's correction request on a closed invoice. One review_reports row per reviewed invoice (review_reports.invoice_id is the invoice that was audited — the PRIOR revision once a resubmission exists) and one review_report_lines row per line the auditor wants changed. disposition is the AUDITOR's verdict on the invoice — APPROVED or CORRECTIONS_REQUESTED — and says nothing about what the supplier did (that is invoices.supplier_acceptance; see supplier response). A review with no corrections is APPROVED, so APPROVED is rare by construction. Lines have no kind column: a RATE correction has requested_rate set and remove_requested = 0; a REMOVAL has remove_requested = 1. requested_rate is a dollar unit rate — always the supplier's active contract rate for the line's item — never a percentage.
- supplier response (aka supplier acceptance, accepted the correction, accepted our corrections, applied the correction, applied the corrections, ignored the correction, ignored our corrections, resubmitted invoice, did they fix it): What the supplier did about a review — recorded on the invoices table, in two places, and nowhere else (there is no supplier_acceptance table and no revisions table). (1) The successor revision: a resubmission is a new invoices row with the same supplier_id and invoice_number, revision + 1, and prior_revision_id pointing at the reviewed invoice; its invoice_lines are what the supplier actually billed after the review. (2) invoices.supplier_acceptance on the REVIEWED (prior) invoice: ACCEPTED when every requested correction was applied on the successor, REJECTED when any one was ignored — written only when a successor arrives, so a review that never drew a resubmission leaves it NULL. About 40% of reviews never draw a resubmission: NULL is "no response yet", not a rejection, and absence of a revision is not refusal.

## Canonical metrics (use these definitions)
- flag_rate: Share of invoices with at least one finding. Engine-defined: InvoiceGuard stores findings but names no such rate.
  tables: invoices, findings
  aggregation: COUNT(DISTINCT f.invoice_id) * 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM invoices)
  notes: Join findings f ON f.invoice_id = invoices.id. For a "substantive" variant exclude bookkeeping rows with f.category NOT IN ('NOTE'). Window on invoices.received_at.
- item_flag_rate: Share of a given item code's lines flagged by a given rule — the shape behind "is item X usually flagged?".
  tables: invoice_lines, findings
  filter: l.item_code = :item_code
  aggregation: AVG(CASE WHEN f.id IS NOT NULL THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END)
  notes: LEFT JOIN findings f ON f.invoice_id = l.invoice_id AND f.line_number = l.line_number AND f.rule_name = :rule_name. Line-level findings join on BOTH invoice_id and line_number.
- recovered_opportunity (aka savings realized, realized savings, realized, savings per auditor, auditor savings, how much has each auditor saved): Opportunity dollars on completed reviews, per team per day — the audit-yield analog, matching the app's production-rollup dashboard exactly.
  tables: invoice_history, users, invoices
  filter: invoice_history.to_status IN ('CLOSED', 'NO_REVIEW_NEEDED')
  aggregation: SUM(COALESCE(invoices.opportunity, 0))
  notes: JOIN users ON users.short_name = invoice_history.actor JOIN invoices ON invoices.id = invoice_history.invoice_id; GROUP BY users.team, DATE(invoice_history.at). This mirrors the app's PRODUCTION_ROLLUP_SQL (platform/api/teams.py).
  interpretations (the answer must name the one used):
    - closed-invoice opportunity: SUM(invoices.opportunity) over reviews the auditor completed — the app's production rollup, the default.
    - closed-invoice findings: effective finding amounts (valid exceptions zeroed) on invoices the auditor closed.
    - feedback-authored findings: effective finding amounts where the auditor authored the finding_feedback row.
- rule_savings (aka savings, most savings, savings by rule, productive, most productive, opportunity by rule, recovery by rule): Effective savings each rule has produced — finding amounts with valid exceptions zeroed, the app's own accounting. Engine- defined; the "which rule saves the most / is most productive" question.
  tables: findings, finding_feedback
  aggregation: SUM(CASE WHEN ff.valid_exception = 1 THEN 0 ELSE COALESCE(f.amount, 0) END)
  notes: The LEFT JOIN is mandatory: filtering ff.valid_exception in the WHERE clause turns it into an INNER JOIN and drops every finding without a feedback row — the inversion the 4b baseline caught (duplicate_line $11K instead of quantity_spike $610K). Zero the excepted rows inside the SUM, never in WHERE. Per-rule AVERAGES are finding-level: AVG over findings.amount, never AVG(invoices.opportunity) across a join — invoice-level values are inflated by every other rule on the same invoice (1.5–25× in the play session).
  interpretations (the answer must name the one used):
    - finding-level: SUM/AVG over findings.amount — the dollars the rule's own findings carry; the default.
    - invoice-level: aggregates over invoices.opportunity for invoices the rule touched — inflated by every co-occurring rule; name it if deliberately used.
- queue_backlog: The READY backlog awaiting audit: count, total opportunity, total weight (the app's queue-health dashboard).
  tables: invoices
  filter: invoices.status = 'READY'
  aggregation: COUNT(*), SUM(COALESCE(invoices.opportunity, 0)), SUM(COALESCE(invoices.weight, 0))
  notes: The app splits this per team by mapping finding categories to teams via config.values_json team_to_categories — a JSON config lookup, not a column; per-team splits need that mapping.
- creepback_suppliers (aka who crept back, raised prices back up after accepting, reinflated prices, crept back up): Suppliers caught creeping prices back up — the creepback scan's own findings, already net of acceptance history.
  tables: findings, invoices, suppliers
  filter: f.rule_name LIKE '%creepback%'
  aggregation: COUNT(*)
  notes: The scan has already verified the accept-then-drift pattern before writing the finding. Layering supplier_acceptance, review_reports.disposition, or invoice_history predicates on top re-tests what the finding already proves and self-annihilates to zero rows (S6: five reps, five empty results). The findings ARE the creep-back population.
- auditor_throughput: Claims and completed reviews per auditor over a half-open [start, end) window (the app's auditor-performance dashboard).
  tables: invoice_history, users
  filter: invoice_history.at >= :start AND invoice_history.at < :end
  aggregation: SUM(CASE WHEN invoice_history.to_status = 'CLAIMED' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), SUM(CASE WHEN invoice_history.to_status IN ('CLOSED', 'NO_REVIEW_NEEDED')
    THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
  notes: JOIN users ON users.short_name = invoice_history.actor; GROUP BY invoice_history.actor. System actors (system.rollup, system.stale-sweep, system.line-mapping) are not auditors — filter users.role = 'auditor'.
- requested_rate_is_contract_rate (aka what rate do they ask for, what rate do auditors ask for, rate do they ask for, rate auditors request, rate we request, requested rate, corrected rate, rate they ask suppliers to charge): The rate auditors ask suppliers to correct to — a dollar unit rate (review_report_lines.requested_rate), and always the supplier's active contract rate for the line's item. The answer to "what rate do they ask for" is "the contract rate", shown as the count of rate corrections that match it beside the total, or as the requested rates themselves. Not a percentage of anything.
  tables: review_report_lines, review_reports, invoices, invoice_lines, contracts
  filter: rrl.requested_rate IS NOT NULL AND rrl.remove_requested = 0
  aggregation: COUNT(DISTINCT rrl.id), COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN c.contract_rate = rrl.requested_rate THEN rrl.id END)
  notes: contracts is versioned — several rows per (supplier_id, item_code); c.effective_to IS NULL pins the active one, otherwise the join doubles the superseded pairs. COUNT(DISTINCT rrl.id), never COUNT(*), over these joins.
- correction_application_rate (aka apply the corrections we request, apply our corrections, corrections applied, applied corrections, correction application, marked as applied, act on our corrections, comply with corrections, correction compliance): Share of requested corrections the supplier actually applied on the resubmission. Population: review_report_lines whose reviewed invoice has a successor revision — a correction never resubmitted against cannot be judged and is not "ignored". Applied: for a RATE correction the successor's same-numbered line bills exactly requested_rate or is gone; for a REMOVAL the line is gone. The ignored lines are exactly the correction_ignored findings, so applied + ignored = population and the three figures agree.
  tables: review_report_lines, review_reports, invoices, invoice_lines
  aggregation: SUM(CASE WHEN <the successor line applied the correction> THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / COUNT(*)
  notes: The successor line is tested with NOT EXISTS, not a LEFT JOIN — the composite line join is the shape the fan-out check challenges. review_reports.disposition is the auditor's verdict and answers nothing about the supplier (APPROVED / all reviews = 1/109 in this data — the wrong answer). application_rate is a fraction; the UI renders it as a percentage.
  interpretations (the answer must name the one used):
    - per correction: correction lines applied / correction lines with a resubmission — the default (55/73 here).
    - per review: reviews whose resubmission applied everything (invoices.supplier_acceptance = 'ACCEPTED') / reviews with a resubmission (supplier_acceptance IS NOT NULL) — 44/61 here; name it if used.
- corrections_ignored_by_supplier (aka ignores our corrections, ignored our corrections, ignores corrections, ignored corrections, corrections ignored, ignored the most corrections, disregards our corrections, did not apply corrections): How many requested corrections each supplier ignored on its resubmission — the app's own correction_ignored findings, one per ignored correction line, written on the SUCCESSOR invoice (amount 0, category CORRECTION).
  tables: findings, invoices, suppliers
  filter: f.rule_name = 'correction_ignored'
  aggregation: COUNT(*)
  notes: The finding is the unit and already encodes the applied-vs-ignored comparison. Counting reviewed invoices that were never ACCEPTED counts the ~40% of reviews that drew no resubmission as ignored (28 for the leading supplier where 9 corrections were ignored, in a world with 18 ignored corrections in total). Counting invoices with supplier_acceptance = 'REJECTED' counts resubmissions, not corrections (one resubmission can ignore two). Use the findings.
- corrections_ignored_by_auditor (aka audit rejections by reviewer, audit rejections, rejections by reviewer, rejections by auditor, ignored corrections by auditor, ignored corrections by reviewer, corrections ignored per auditor): Ignored corrections attributed to the auditor who requested them. Neither findings nor review_reports carry a reviewer column: the requesting auditor is the actor who CLOSED the reviewed (prior) revision — from the correction_ignored finding's invoice (the successor) to its prior_revision_id, then that prior's invoice_history row with to_status = 'CLOSED' (exactly one per invoice). actor is a users.short_name.
  tables: findings, invoices, invoice_history, users
  filter: f.rule_name = 'correction_ignored' AND h.to_status = 'CLOSED'
  aggregation: COUNT(*)
  notes: "Rejection" here is the supplier rejecting the auditor's correction — the default reading. There is no REJECTED invoice status: invoice_history.to_status holds only the seven lifecycle states and review_reports.disposition only APPROVED / CORRECTIONS_REQUESTED. The closer is looked up in a scalar subquery so the aggregate scope carries no join to invoice_history. Join users on users.short_name = reviewer for names or teams.
  interpretations (the answer must name the one used):
    - ignored corrections: correction_ignored findings per requesting auditor — the supplier rejected the correction; the default.
    - corrections requested: review_reports with disposition = 'CORRECTIONS_REQUESTED' per auditor who closed the reviewed invoice — the auditor rejected the invoice as billed; name it if used.

## Canonical join paths
- invoices_to_lines: invoices.id = invoice_lines.invoice_id
- invoices_to_findings: invoices.id = findings.invoice_id (Invoice-level findings have line_number NULL.)
- lines_to_findings: invoice_lines.invoice_id = findings.invoice_id; invoice_lines.line_number = findings.line_number (Composite join — line-level findings match on BOTH columns; joining on invoice_id alone cross-multiplies lines with the invoice's other findings.)
- findings_to_feedback: findings.id = finding_feedback.finding_id (At most one feedback row per finding (finding_id is unique).)
- invoices_to_suppliers: invoices.supplier_id = suppliers.id
- invoices_to_claimer: invoices.claimed_by = users.id (claimed_by is a user id; invoice_history.actor is a user short_name (string) — two different keys for people.)
- invoices_to_history: invoices.id = invoice_history.invoice_id
- suppliers_to_contracts: suppliers.id = contracts.supplier_id (The active contract for a line also matches item_code and the date window effective_from <= at < effective_to (open-ended when effective_to is NULL); several revisions of a contract can exist per (supplier, item).)
- invoices_to_compliance: invoices.id = compliance_reports.invoice_id; compliance_reports.id = compliance_rules.compliance_report_id (Compliance findings (rule_name compliance_<code>) correspond one-to-one to compliance_rules rows, whose severity is the authority. Joining findings to compliance_rules through invoice_id pairs every finding with every rule on the invoice — count compliance_rules directly for severity questions.)
- invoice_to_successor: invoices.id = invoices.prior_revision_id (succ.prior_revision_id = inv.id, a self-join. A reviewed invoice has at most one successor (UNIQUE supplier_id, invoice_number, revision; a resubmission is revision + 1), so the join multiplies rows in neither direction. The successor carries the correction_ignored findings; the prior carries supplier_acceptance.)
- reviews_to_invoices: review_reports.invoice_id = invoices.id (The reviewed invoice — the prior revision once a resubmission exists.)
- review_lines_to_reviews: review_report_lines.review_report_id = review_reports.id
- review_lines_to_billed_lines: review_report_lines.line_number = invoice_lines.line_number (Composite — always AND an invoice: il.invoice_id = the reviewed invoice (what was billed before the review) or = its successor (what was billed after). line_number alone repeats on every invoice. Inside an aggregate, test the successor line with EXISTS / NOT EXISTS (the correction_application_rate template) rather than a LEFT JOIN the fan-out check will challenge.)
- successor_to_requesting_auditor: invoices.prior_revision_id = invoices.id; invoices.id = invoice_history.invoice_id (Filter invoice_history.to_status = 'CLOSED' — one row per invoice, the auditor who closed the review; actor is a users.short_name. Neither findings nor review_reports name a reviewer.)

## Gotchas (read before writing SQL)
- adjustment_totals: invoice_total legitimately differs from the sum of lines when adjustments exist — a silent mismatch is not an error.
  When invoices.adjustment_flag = 1, the stated invoice_total is deliberately below SUM(invoice_lines.extended_price) (supplier- side credits and adjustments, typically 50-500), and the total_mismatch rule deliberately stays silent. A separate, smaller population carries genuine unexplained mismatches (typically 5-50) with adjustment_flag = 0, and those ARE flagged as total_mismatch findings. Never validate invoice_total against the line sum without checking adjustment_flag first. To count the silent-adjustment population: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM invoices i WHERE i.adjustment_flag = 1 AND ABS(i.invoice_total - (SELECT SUM(l.extended_price) FROM invoice_lines l WHERE l.invoice_id = i.id)) > 0.01 AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM findings f WHERE f.invoice_id = i.id AND f.rule_name = 'total_mismatch').
- data_coverage: The data covers 2026-03-02 through 2026-05-30 — never use date('now') or CURRENT_DATE in queries.
  This is a simulated world: activity runs 2026-03-02 to 2026-05-30 and nothing is newer. Relative phrases like "last week" anchor to the data's end (the last received_at day is 2026-05-29; scheduled tasks run through 2026-05-30), not to today. For received_at windows last_day is 2026-05-29 (the 05-30 in the coverage line is scheduled-task activity). A relative window of N days ends on that last day, inclusive, as a half-open range [last_day - N + 1, last_day + 1): "last 7 days" / "last week" / "this week" are all received_at >= '2026-05-23 00:00:00' AND received_at < '2026-05-30 00:00:00' — a week is always this trailing window, never a calendar (Sun–Sat or Mon–Sun) week, because the last day falls mid-week and week-start conventions differ; "last 30 days" is received_at >= '2026-04-30 00:00:00' AND received_at < '2026-05-30 00:00:00'. "This month" is the calendar month containing the last day — the reporting unit, and complete, since 2026-05-29 is May's last business day: received_at >= '2026-05-01 00:00:00' AND received_at < '2026-06-01 00:00:00'. Windows on invoice_history.at and compliance_reports.issued_at anchor the same way. Invoices arrive on business days only — weekends have no received_at values, though daily sweeps still log.
- naive_datetime_strings: Datetimes are naive-UTC strings; booleans are 0/1 integers.
  Datetime columns store 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.ffffff' with no timezone (UTC by convention). Compare against full string literals ('2026-05-23 00:00:00' works; date('now') does not belong here at all). Boolean columns (adjustment_flag, rush_flag, is_credit_memo, disputed_hold, network, available) store 0/1.
- null_amount_findings: findings.amount is NULL for flat flag-style findings — SUM over amounts silently skips them, and excepted findings still carry their original amount.
  Flag-style rules (new_supplier, split_billing, line_note) write amount NULL: they mark risk, not dollars. And when an auditor marks a finding a valid exception (finding_feedback. valid_exception = 1), the app treats its effective amount as 0 — but findings.amount keeps the original value. Dollar aggregations that should reflect the app's numbers must LEFT JOIN finding_feedback and zero out excepted rows.
- rate_needs_unflagged_side: A rate over a population needs the unflagged side — COALESCE(indicator, 0) (or a CASE) so AVG doesn't silently skip NULLs and saturate to 1.0.
  "Usually", "share of", "what rate" questions divide by the WHOLE population, but building the indicator via a LEFT JOIN leaves unmatched rows NULL, and AVG skips NULLs — every unflagged line vanishes from the denominator and the rate saturates to exactly 1.0 (the pin pass's S2: 1.0 reported where the true rate was 63/66). Make the unflagged side an explicit 0: AVG(COALESCE(indicator, 0)), or SUM(CASE WHEN <match> THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / COUNT(*) over the population rows in ONE scope — never a COUNT of matches in one query divided by a COUNT of the population in another: a scalar-subquery pair or two joined COUNTs is the fan-out shape the lint challenges and the Verifier marks unverified (the post-Block-2 S2 overrides, and rep 5's 1.0476 = 66 lines under a fanned 69). The indicator itself is CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM findings f WHERE f.invoice_id = l.invoice_id AND f.line_number = l.line_number AND f.rule_name = '<rule>') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END per population row — the correction_application_rate template's shape, which never meets the fan-out check. Never a LEFT JOIN indicator: <match>.id IS NOT NULL over a joined findings row is the composite line join the fan-out check challenges (a line may carry more than one finding by schema, so the join is not declared one-to-one), and never a COUNT(<match>.id) grouped per row: a count is not an indicator (a row with two matches counts 2 and the "rate" runs past 1.0).
- compliance_dual_signal: Critical compliance uses two deliberately different signals — the weight boost reads finding amounts, sweep protection reads the denormalized column.
  The roll-up's flat weight boost fires when the SUM of COMPLIANCE finding amounts reaches the critical threshold (1500); stale-sweep protection instead reads invoices.compliance_score (denormalized from the compliance report). Excepting a compliance finding removes the boost but not the protection — the two questions have different answers by design.
- no_closed_at_column: invoices has no closed/worked timestamp — completion times live in invoice_history.
  To answer when an invoice was claimed or closed, join invoice_history and filter to_status ('CLAIMED', 'CLOSED', 'NO_REVIEW_NEEDED') using invoice_history.at. received_at and scored_at are the only timestamps on invoices.
- status_is_current: invoices.status is the current state only — past states and reactivations live in invoice_history.
  An invoice that was LAPSED and later reactivated is no longer LAPSED: its status now reads CLAIMED, IN_REVIEW, or CLOSED. Filtering invoices.status = 'LAPSED' therefore excludes exactly the reactivated population. "Has an invoice ever been X" or "was reactivated / moved out of X" is a transition question: SELECT invoice_history.actor, invoices.invoice_number FROM invoice_history JOIN invoices ON invoices.id = invoice_history.invoice_id WHERE invoice_history.from_status = 'LAPSED' — no filter on the current status. The sanctioned reactivation is performed by an audit manager (users.role = 'audit_manager'); actor holds the user's short_name.
- time_in_status: Time in a status pairs the transition that ENTERS it (to_status = X) with the one that LEAVES it (from_status = X) — two different invoice_history rows.
  invoice_history rows are transitions, not states. "How long from RECEIVED to READY" is the gap between the row entering RECEIVED (to_status = 'RECEIVED') and the row leaving it (from_status = 'RECEIVED' AND to_status = 'READY'), joined per invoice_id. Reading both timestamps from the single READY transition row (CASE branches over from_status/to_status inside a WHERE to_status = 'READY' scope) subtracts a timestamp from itself and yields exactly 0:00:00 — the play session's W3. Units: leaving.at - entering.at is an INTERVAL, not a number. Scale it only after EPOCH — AVG(EPOCH(lv.at - en.at)) / 3600.0 AS avg_hours — or count units with DATE_DIFF('hour', en.at, lv.at). AVG(lv.at - en.at) / 86400 AS avg_time_in_days (the post-coverage W3) divides an interval by a number and yields an interval of 0.041667 seconds, not 0.0417 days.
- rule_name_prefixes: findings.rule_name drops the code's rule_ prefix, and compliance findings are named compliance_<rule code> — a naming convention, never a join key.
  The rules engine's rule_rate_variance writes rule_name 'rate_variance', and so on. Compliance-intake findings arrive as compliance_CR-147 etc. — filtering rule_name LIKE 'compliance_%' selects exactly the compliance layer. But rule_name = 'compliance_' || rule_code is a DERIVED, NON-UNIQUE key (10 rule codes across 4,216 compliance_rules rows): used as a join condition it pairs every finding of a code with every rule of that code and fans out 17× and worse. Never join on it. For severity questions count compliance_rules directly — the invoices_to_compliance join path is the keyed road when invoice context is needed.
- rate_means_dollars_here: In review and contract context "rate" is a dollar unit rate (requested_rate, contract_rate, unit_rate), not a percentage.
  "What rate do auditors ask for", "the rate we requested", "the corrected rate" are dollars-per-unit questions answered from review_report_lines.requested_rate (see requested_rate_is_contract_rate) — never a share of findings. Percentage questions say "share", "how often", "what fraction", "what percent", and divide a count by its population; flag_rate, item_flag_rate and correction_application_rate are that kind. findings.category = 'CORRECTION' is the correction_ignored findings, and its share of all findings answers no rate question of either kind.
- corrections_never_resubmitted: A review that never drew a resubmission is neither applied nor ignored — leave it out of application rates and never count it as a rejection.
  109 reviews; 61 drew a resubmission (invoices.supplier_acceptance set on the reviewed invoice), 48 did not (supplier_acceptance NULL). Applied and ignored are judged only where a successor exists: 73 correction lines with a successor = 55 applied + 18 ignored, and the 18 are exactly the correction_ignored findings. Counting the 48 unanswered reviews as ignored, or reading review_reports.disposition (the auditor's verdict) as the supplier's response, overstates or inverts the answer. The per-line figure counts RATE and REMOVAL corrections alike; the rate-only subset (48 lines, 34 applied) is not the headline.

## Where to look
- Q: How many invoices received last week had findings?
  Join invoices to findings on invoice_id — an inner join: a LEFT JOIN counts every received invoice, not the flagged ones; COUNT(DISTINCT invoices.id); window on invoices.received_at anchored to the data's end (see data_coverage — "last week" means the final seven days ending 2026-05-30, i.e. received_at >= '2026-05-23 00:00:00' AND received_at < '2026-05-30 00:00:00').
- Q: Which supplier draws the most rate-variance findings?
  findings WHERE rule_name = 'rate_variance', joined through invoices to suppliers; GROUP BY suppliers.code ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC. Rate variance is the planted specialty of one supplier, so expect a dominant leader.
- Q: Is a given service item usually flagged for excessive hours?
  Use item_flag_rate with rule_name = 'service_hours_excessive' over invoice_lines filtered to the item_code — remember the composite line-level join (lines_to_findings).
- Q: Who closes the most reviews?
  auditor_throughput over invoice_history: to_status IN ('CLOSED', 'NO_REVIEW_NEEDED') GROUP BY actor, joined to users on short_name and filtered to role = 'auditor'.
- Q: How much recovery opportunity did each team close last month?
  recovered_opportunity per team/day (PRODUCTION_ROLLUP_SQL shape), windowed on invoice_history.at — anchored to the data's end, per data_coverage.
- Q: When auditors request corrections, what rate do they ask for?
  Dollars, not a percentage (rate_means_dollars_here): requested_rate_is_contract_rate — the answer is "the contract rate", shown as rate corrections at the contract rate beside the total, with the lowest and highest requested rates. Never the share of findings in category CORRECTION.
- Q: How often do suppliers actually apply the corrections we request?
  correction_application_rate (per correction, the default; name the reading). review_reports.disposition is the auditor's verdict on the invoice and says nothing about the supplier — APPROVED / all reviews is the wrong answer by two orders of magnitude.
- Q: Which supplier ignores our corrections the most, and how many?
  corrections_ignored_by_supplier — the correction_ignored findings, never a count of reviews or invoices without ACCEPTED (that counts reviews the supplier never answered).
- Q: List audit rejections by reviewer.
  corrections_ignored_by_auditor (ignored corrections per requesting auditor, the default; name the reading). REJECTED is not an invoice status: to_status never holds it, and review_reports.disposition holds only APPROVED / CORRECTIONS_REQUESTED. The reviewer is the actor who CLOSED the prior revision.
- Q: Show total invoiced amount per supplier, including suppliers with no invoice lines.
  LEFT JOIN from suppliers and SUM(invoices.invoice_total) with no COALESCE: suppliers with no invoices, and out-of-network suppliers whose invoices are born LAPSED with NULL totals and no lines, come back NULL — rendered as a dash, which is the truth ("nothing to sum"), where $0.00 asserts they invoiced nothing.

## Business concepts
- invoice lifecycle (aka status, queue state): An invoice moves RECEIVED -> READY -> CLAIMED -> IN_REVIEW -> CLOSED or NO_REVIEW_NEEDED; unworked invoices past the lapse window become LAPSED. Every transition is a row in invoice_history (from_status, to_status, actor, at); the invoices table stores only the current status.
- finding (aka flag, rule hit): One rule hit on an invoice (or one of its lines). rule_name is the rule that fired (rate_variance, total_mismatch, ...; compliance findings are named compliance_<rule code>); category routes it to a team (MATERIAL/SERVICE/FEE/COMPLIANCE/CORRECTION/ CREEPBACK/NOTE); amount is the dollar impact, NULL for flat flag-style findings.
- opportunity (aka recovery opportunity, dollars on the table, savings, productivity): The recovery dollars an audit of this invoice might yield — the sum of effective finding amounts plus (when larger than the service findings) the benchmark service-hours delta priced at the contract labor rate. Stored on invoices.opportunity by the roll-up.
- weight (aka priority, score): Queue priority: opportunity-derived, multiplied for creep-back (x2) and ignored corrections (x5), boosted flat for critical compliance, then divided by invoice total — density of opportunity per review hour, not raw dollars. Stored on invoices.weight.
- revision chain (aka resubmission): A resubmitted invoice arrives as a new row with the same (supplier_id, invoice_number) and revision + 1, linked by prior_revision_id. supplier_acceptance records whether the supplier ACCEPTED or REJECTED the prior review's requested changes.
- creep-back (aka creepback, creep back, raised prices back up, reinflation, price creep): A supplier accepts a corrected rate on one revision, then quietly drifts the price back up on a later one. Detected by the creepback scan; lands as CREEPBACK findings and doubles the invoice's weight multiplier.
- lapse (aka stale, expiry): Invoices still RECEIVED/READY past the lapse window (lapse_after_days, default 6, plus one fixed grace day) are swept to LAPSED by the daily stale sweep — unless protected by a critical compliance score (invoices.compliance_score >= 1500).
- network supplier: suppliers.network = 1 means in-network: their invoices enter the audit pipeline. Out-of-network suppliers' invoices are born LAPSED (out of audit scope), not scored. Those invoices carry NULL invoice_total and no invoice_lines — a total over them is NULL (no data, rendered as a dash), never $0 — and two suppliers have no invoices at all.
- audit rules (aka rules, audit rule): "Rules" has three senses. (1) The 12 audit rules in the rules engine's code — every one runs on every scored invoice, so "how many rules run on an invoice" is 12, answered from the primer/CKG, not SQL. (2) Compliance rule codes — compliance_rules rows, severity-bearing, arriving as compliance_<code> findings; 10 distinct rule codes in this data. (3) findings.rule_name values — the rules that actually FIRED (26 distinct values, since compliance findings arrive as compliance_<code>). Counting compliance_reports per invoice answers none of these.
- review report (aka corrections we request, corrections we requested, requested corrections, correction request, correction requests, audit adjustments, what we asked them to change, auditor corrections): An auditor's correction request on a closed invoice. One review_reports row per reviewed invoice (review_reports.invoice_id is the invoice that was audited — the PRIOR revision once a resubmission exists) and one review_report_lines row per line the auditor wants changed. disposition is the AUDITOR's verdict on the invoice — APPROVED or CORRECTIONS_REQUESTED — and says nothing about what the supplier did (that is invoices.supplier_acceptance; see supplier response). A review with no corrections is APPROVED, so APPROVED is rare by construction. Lines have no kind column: a RATE correction has requested_rate set and remove_requested = 0; a REMOVAL has remove_requested = 1. requested_rate is a dollar unit rate — always the supplier's active contract rate for the line's item — never a percentage.
- supplier response (aka supplier acceptance, accepted the correction, accepted our corrections, applied the correction, applied the corrections, ignored the correction, ignored our corrections, resubmitted invoice, did they fix it): What the supplier did about a review — recorded on the invoices table, in two places, and nowhere else (there is no supplier_acceptance table and no revisions table). (1) The successor revision: a resubmission is a new invoices row with the same supplier_id and invoice_number, revision + 1, and prior_revision_id pointing at the reviewed invoice; its invoice_lines are what the supplier actually billed after the review. (2) invoices.supplier_acceptance on the REVIEWED (prior) invoice: ACCEPTED when every requested correction was applied on the successor, REJECTED when any one was ignored — written only when a successor arrives, so a review that never drew a resubmission leaves it NULL. About 40% of reviews never draw a resubmission: NULL is "no response yet", not a rejection, and absence of a revision is not refusal.

## Canonical metrics (use these definitions)
- flag_rate: Share of invoices with at least one finding. Engine-defined: InvoiceGuard stores findings but names no such rate.
  tables: invoices, findings
  aggregation: COUNT(DISTINCT f.invoice_id) * 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM invoices)
  notes: Join findings f ON f.invoice_id = invoices.id. For a "substantive" variant exclude bookkeeping rows with f.category NOT IN ('NOTE'). Window on invoices.received_at.
- item_flag_rate: Share of a given item code's lines flagged by a given rule — the shape behind "is item X usually flagged?".
  tables: invoice_lines, findings
  filter: l.item_code = :item_code
  aggregation: AVG(CASE WHEN f.id IS NOT NULL THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END)
  notes: LEFT JOIN findings f ON f.invoice_id = l.invoice_id AND f.line_number = l.line_number AND f.rule_name = :rule_name. Line-level findings join on BOTH invoice_id and line_number.
- recovered_opportunity (aka savings realized, realized savings, realized, savings per auditor, auditor savings, how much has each auditor saved): Opportunity dollars on completed reviews, per team per day — the audit-yield analog, matching the app's production-rollup dashboard exactly.
  tables: invoice_history, users, invoices
  filter: invoice_history.to_status IN ('CLOSED', 'NO_REVIEW_NEEDED')
  aggregation: SUM(COALESCE(invoices.opportunity, 0))
  notes: JOIN users ON users.short_name = invoice_history.actor JOIN invoices ON invoices.id = invoice_history.invoice_id; GROUP BY users.team, DATE(invoice_history.at). This mirrors the app's PRODUCTION_ROLLUP_SQL (platform/api/teams.py).
  interpretations (the answer must name the one used):
    - closed-invoice opportunity: SUM(invoices.opportunity) over reviews the auditor completed — the app's production rollup, the default.
    - closed-invoice findings: effective finding amounts (valid exceptions zeroed) on invoices the auditor closed.
    - feedback-authored findings: effective finding amounts where the auditor authored the finding_feedback row.
- rule_savings (aka savings, most savings, savings by rule, productive, most productive, opportunity by rule, recovery by rule): Effective savings each rule has produced — finding amounts with valid exceptions zeroed, the app's own accounting. Engine- defined; the "which rule saves the most / is most productive" question.
  tables: findings, finding_feedback
  aggregation: SUM(CASE WHEN ff.valid_exception = 1 THEN 0 ELSE COALESCE(f.amount, 0) END)
  notes: The LEFT JOIN is mandatory: filtering ff.valid_exception in the WHERE clause turns it into an INNER JOIN and drops every finding without a feedback row — the inversion the 4b baseline caught (duplicate_line $11K instead of quantity_spike $610K). Zero the excepted rows inside the SUM, never in WHERE. Per-rule AVERAGES are finding-level: AVG over findings.amount, never AVG(invoices.opportunity) across a join — invoice-level values are inflated by every other rule on the same invoice (1.5–25× in the play session).
  interpretations (the answer must name the one used):
    - finding-level: SUM/AVG over findings.amount — the dollars the rule's own findings carry; the default.
    - invoice-level: aggregates over invoices.opportunity for invoices the rule touched — inflated by every co-occurring rule; name it if deliberately used.
- queue_backlog: The READY backlog awaiting audit: count, total opportunity, total weight (the app's queue-health dashboard).
  tables: invoices
  filter: invoices.status = 'READY'
  aggregation: COUNT(*), SUM(COALESCE(invoices.opportunity, 0)), SUM(COALESCE(invoices.weight, 0))
  notes: The app splits this per team by mapping finding categories to teams via config.values_json team_to_categories — a JSON config lookup, not a column; per-team splits need that mapping.
- creepback_suppliers (aka who crept back, raised prices back up after accepting, reinflated prices, crept back up): Suppliers caught creeping prices back up — the creepback scan's own findings, already net of acceptance history.
  tables: findings, invoices, suppliers
  filter: f.rule_name LIKE '%creepback%'
  aggregation: COUNT(*)
  notes: The scan has already verified the accept-then-drift pattern before writing the finding. Layering supplier_acceptance, review_reports.disposition, or invoice_history predicates on top re-tests what the finding already proves and self-annihilates to zero rows (S6: five reps, five empty results). The findings ARE the creep-back population.
- auditor_throughput: Claims and completed reviews per auditor over a half-open [start, end) window (the app's auditor-performance dashboard).
  tables: invoice_history, users
  filter: invoice_history.at >= :start AND invoice_history.at < :end
  aggregation: SUM(CASE WHEN invoice_history.to_status = 'CLAIMED' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), SUM(CASE WHEN invoice_history.to_status IN ('CLOSED', 'NO_REVIEW_NEEDED')
    THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
  notes: JOIN users ON users.short_name = invoice_history.actor; GROUP BY invoice_history.actor. System actors (system.rollup, system.stale-sweep, system.line-mapping) are not auditors — filter users.role = 'auditor'.
- requested_rate_is_contract_rate (aka what rate do they ask for, what rate do auditors ask for, rate do they ask for, rate auditors request, rate we request, requested rate, corrected rate, rate they ask suppliers to charge): The rate auditors ask suppliers to correct to — a dollar unit rate (review_report_lines.requested_rate), and always the supplier's active contract rate for the line's item. The answer to "what rate do they ask for" is "the contract rate", shown as the count of rate corrections that match it beside the total, or as the requested rates themselves. Not a percentage of anything.
  tables: review_report_lines, review_reports, invoices, invoice_lines, contracts
  filter: rrl.requested_rate IS NOT NULL AND rrl.remove_requested = 0
  aggregation: COUNT(DISTINCT rrl.id), COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN c.contract_rate = rrl.requested_rate THEN rrl.id END)
  notes: contracts is versioned — several rows per (supplier_id, item_code); c.effective_to IS NULL pins the active one, otherwise the join doubles the superseded pairs. COUNT(DISTINCT rrl.id), never COUNT(*), over these joins.
- correction_application_rate (aka apply the corrections we request, apply our corrections, corrections applied, applied corrections, correction application, marked as applied, act on our corrections, comply with corrections, correction compliance): Share of requested corrections the supplier actually applied on the resubmission. Population: review_report_lines whose reviewed invoice has a successor revision — a correction never resubmitted against cannot be judged and is not "ignored". Applied: for a RATE correction the successor's same-numbered line bills exactly requested_rate or is gone; for a REMOVAL the line is gone. The ignored lines are exactly the correction_ignored findings, so applied + ignored = population and the three figures agree.
  tables: review_report_lines, review_reports, invoices, invoice_lines
  aggregation: SUM(CASE WHEN <the successor line applied the correction> THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / COUNT(*)
  notes: The successor line is tested with NOT EXISTS, not a LEFT JOIN — the composite line join is the shape the fan-out check challenges. review_reports.disposition is the auditor's verdict and answers nothing about the supplier (APPROVED / all reviews = 1/109 in this data — the wrong answer). application_rate is a fraction; the UI renders it as a percentage.
  interpretations (the answer must name the one used):
    - per correction: correction lines applied / correction lines with a resubmission — the default (55/73 here).
    - per review: reviews whose resubmission applied everything (invoices.supplier_acceptance = 'ACCEPTED') / reviews with a resubmission (supplier_acceptance IS NOT NULL) — 44/61 here; name it if used.
- corrections_ignored_by_supplier (aka ignores our corrections, ignored our corrections, ignores corrections, ignored corrections, corrections ignored, ignored the most corrections, disregards our corrections, did not apply corrections): How many requested corrections each supplier ignored on its resubmission — the app's own correction_ignored findings, one per ignored correction line, written on the SUCCESSOR invoice (amount 0, category CORRECTION).
  tables: findings, invoices, suppliers
  filter: f.rule_name = 'correction_ignored'
  aggregation: COUNT(*)
  notes: The finding is the unit and already encodes the applied-vs-ignored comparison. Counting reviewed invoices that were never ACCEPTED counts the ~40% of reviews that drew no resubmission as ignored (28 for the leading supplier where 9 corrections were ignored, in a world with 18 ignored corrections in total). Counting invoices with supplier_acceptance = 'REJECTED' counts resubmissions, not corrections (one resubmission can ignore two). Use the findings.
- corrections_ignored_by_auditor (aka audit rejections by reviewer, audit rejections, rejections by reviewer, rejections by auditor, ignored corrections by auditor, ignored corrections by reviewer, corrections ignored per auditor): Ignored corrections attributed to the auditor who requested them. Neither findings nor review_reports carry a reviewer column: the requesting auditor is the actor who CLOSED the reviewed (prior) revision — from the correction_ignored finding's invoice (the successor) to its prior_revision_id, then that prior's invoice_history row with to_status = 'CLOSED' (exactly one per invoice). actor is a users.short_name.
  tables: findings, invoices, invoice_history, users
  filter: f.rule_name = 'correction_ignored' AND h.to_status = 'CLOSED'
  aggregation: COUNT(*)
  notes: "Rejection" here is the supplier rejecting the auditor's correction — the default reading. There is no REJECTED invoice status: invoice_history.to_status holds only the seven lifecycle states and review_reports.disposition only APPROVED / CORRECTIONS_REQUESTED. The closer is looked up in a scalar subquery so the aggregate scope carries no join to invoice_history. Join users on users.short_name = reviewer for names or teams.
  interpretations (the answer must name the one used):
    - ignored corrections: correction_ignored findings per requesting auditor — the supplier rejected the correction; the default.
    - corrections requested: review_reports with disposition = 'CORRECTIONS_REQUESTED' per auditor who closed the reviewed invoice — the auditor rejected the invoice as billed; name it if used.

## Canonical join paths
- invoices_to_lines: invoices.id = invoice_lines.invoice_id
- invoices_to_findings: invoices.id = findings.invoice_id (Invoice-level findings have line_number NULL.)
- lines_to_findings: invoice_lines.invoice_id = findings.invoice_id; invoice_lines.line_number = findings.line_number (Composite join — line-level findings match on BOTH columns; joining on invoice_id alone cross-multiplies lines with the invoice's other findings.)
- findings_to_feedback: findings.id = finding_feedback.finding_id (At most one feedback row per finding (finding_id is unique).)
- invoices_to_suppliers: invoices.supplier_id = suppliers.id
- invoices_to_claimer: invoices.claimed_by = users.id (claimed_by is a user id; invoice_history.actor is a user short_name (string) — two different keys for people.)
- invoices_to_history: invoices.id = invoice_history.invoice_id
- suppliers_to_contracts: suppliers.id = contracts.supplier_id (The active contract for a line also matches item_code and the date window effective_from <= at < effective_to (open-ended when effective_to is NULL); several revisions of a contract can exist per (supplier, item).)
- invoices_to_compliance: invoices.id = compliance_reports.invoice_id; compliance_reports.id = compliance_rules.compliance_report_id (Compliance findings (rule_name compliance_<code>) correspond one-to-one to compliance_rules rows, whose severity is the authority. Joining findings to compliance_rules through invoice_id pairs every finding with every rule on the invoice — count compliance_rules directly for severity questions.)
- invoice_to_successor: invoices.id = invoices.prior_revision_id (succ.prior_revision_id = inv.id, a self-join. A reviewed invoice has at most one successor (UNIQUE supplier_id, invoice_number, revision; a resubmission is revision + 1), so the join multiplies rows in neither direction. The successor carries the correction_ignored findings; the prior carries supplier_acceptance.)
- reviews_to_invoices: review_reports.invoice_id = invoices.id (The reviewed invoice — the prior revision once a resubmission exists.)
- review_lines_to_reviews: review_report_lines.review_report_id = review_reports.id
- review_lines_to_billed_lines: review_report_lines.line_number = invoice_lines.line_number (Composite — always AND an invoice: il.invoice_id = the reviewed invoice (what was billed before the review) or = its successor (what was billed after). line_number alone repeats on every invoice. Inside an aggregate, test the successor line with EXISTS / NOT EXISTS (the correction_application_rate template) rather than a LEFT JOIN the fan-out check will challenge.)
- successor_to_requesting_auditor: invoices.prior_revision_id = invoices.id; invoices.id = invoice_history.invoice_id (Filter invoice_history.to_status = 'CLOSED' — one row per invoice, the auditor who closed the review; actor is a users.short_name. Neither findings nor review_reports name a reviewer.)

## Gotchas (read before writing SQL)
- adjustment_totals: invoice_total legitimately differs from the sum of lines when adjustments exist — a silent mismatch is not an error.
  When invoices.adjustment_flag = 1, the stated invoice_total is deliberately below SUM(invoice_lines.extended_price) (supplier- side credits and adjustments, typically 50-500), and the total_mismatch rule deliberately stays silent. A separate, smaller population carries genuine unexplained mismatches (typically 5-50) with adjustment_flag = 0, and those ARE flagged as total_mismatch findings. Never validate invoice_total against the line sum without checking adjustment_flag first. To count the silent-adjustment population: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM invoices i WHERE i.adjustment_flag = 1 AND ABS(i.invoice_total - (SELECT SUM(l.extended_price) FROM invoice_lines l WHERE l.invoice_id = i.id)) > 0.01 AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM findings f WHERE f.invoice_id = i.id AND f.rule_name = 'total_mismatch').
- data_coverage: The data covers 2026-03-02 through 2026-05-30 — never use date('now') or CURRENT_DATE in queries.
  This is a simulated world: activity runs 2026-03-02 to 2026-05-30 and nothing is newer. Relative phrases like "last week" anchor to the data's end (the last received_at day is 2026-05-29; scheduled tasks run through 2026-05-30), not to today. For received_at windows last_day is 2026-05-29 (the 05-30 in the coverage line is scheduled-task activity). A relative window of N days ends on that last day, inclusive, as a half-open range [last_day - N + 1, last_day + 1): "last 7 days" / "last week" / "this week" are all received_at >= '2026-05-23 00:00:00' AND received_at < '2026-05-30 00:00:00' — a week is always this trailing window, never a calendar (Sun–Sat or Mon–Sun) week, because the last day falls mid-week and week-start conventions differ; "last 30 days" is received_at >= '2026-04-30 00:00:00' AND received_at < '2026-05-30 00:00:00'. "This month" is the calendar month containing the last day — the reporting unit, and complete, since 2026-05-29 is May's last business day: received_at >= '2026-05-01 00:00:00' AND received_at < '2026-06-01 00:00:00'. Windows on invoice_history.at and compliance_reports.issued_at anchor the same way. Invoices arrive on business days only — weekends have no received_at values, though daily sweeps still log.
- naive_datetime_strings: Datetimes are naive-UTC strings; booleans are 0/1 integers.
  Datetime columns store 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.ffffff' with no timezone (UTC by convention). Compare against full string literals ('2026-05-23 00:00:00' works; date('now') does not belong here at all). Boolean columns (adjustment_flag, rush_flag, is_credit_memo, disputed_hold, network, available) store 0/1.
- null_amount_findings: findings.amount is NULL for flat flag-style findings — SUM over amounts silently skips them, and excepted findings still carry their original amount.
  Flag-style rules (new_supplier, split_billing, line_note) write amount NULL: they mark risk, not dollars. And when an auditor marks a finding a valid exception (finding_feedback. valid_exception = 1), the app treats its effective amount as 0 — but findings.amount keeps the original value. Dollar aggregations that should reflect the app's numbers must LEFT JOIN finding_feedback and zero out excepted rows.
- rate_needs_unflagged_side: A rate over a population needs the unflagged side — COALESCE(indicator, 0) (or a CASE) so AVG doesn't silently skip NULLs and saturate to 1.0.
  "Usually", "share of", "what rate" questions divide by the WHOLE population, but building the indicator via a LEFT JOIN leaves unmatched rows NULL, and AVG skips NULLs — every unflagged line vanishes from the denominator and the rate saturates to exactly 1.0 (the pin pass's S2: 1.0 reported where the true rate was 63/66). Make the unflagged side an explicit 0: AVG(COALESCE(indicator, 0)), or SUM(CASE WHEN <match> THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / COUNT(*) over the population rows in ONE scope — never a COUNT of matches in one query divided by a COUNT of the population in another: a scalar-subquery pair or two joined COUNTs is the fan-out shape the lint challenges and the Verifier marks unverified (the post-Block-2 S2 overrides, and rep 5's 1.0476 = 66 lines under a fanned 69). The indicator itself is CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM findings f WHERE f.invoice_id = l.invoice_id AND f.line_number = l.line_number AND f.rule_name = '<rule>') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END per population row — the correction_application_rate template's shape, which never meets the fan-out check. Never a LEFT JOIN indicator: <match>.id IS NOT NULL over a joined findings row is the composite line join the fan-out check challenges (a line may carry more than one finding by schema, so the join is not declared one-to-one), and never a COUNT(<match>.id) grouped per row: a count is not an indicator (a row with two matches counts 2 and the "rate" runs past 1.0).
- compliance_dual_signal: Critical compliance uses two deliberately different signals — the weight boost reads finding amounts, sweep protection reads the denormalized column.
  The roll-up's flat weight boost fires when the SUM of COMPLIANCE finding amounts reaches the critical threshold (1500); stale-sweep protection instead reads invoices.compliance_score (denormalized from the compliance report). Excepting a compliance finding removes the boost but not the protection — the two questions have different answers by design.
- no_closed_at_column: invoices has no closed/worked timestamp — completion times live in invoice_history.
  To answer when an invoice was claimed or closed, join invoice_history and filter to_status ('CLAIMED', 'CLOSED', 'NO_REVIEW_NEEDED') using invoice_history.at. received_at and scored_at are the only timestamps on invoices.
- status_is_current: invoices.status is the current state only — past states and reactivations live in invoice_history.
  An invoice that was LAPSED and later reactivated is no longer LAPSED: its status now reads CLAIMED, IN_REVIEW, or CLOSED. Filtering invoices.status = 'LAPSED' therefore excludes exactly the reactivated population. "Has an invoice ever been X" or "was reactivated / moved out of X" is a transition question: SELECT invoice_history.actor, invoices.invoice_number FROM invoice_history JOIN invoices ON invoices.id = invoice_history.invoice_id WHERE invoice_history.from_status = 'LAPSED' — no filter on the current status. The sanctioned reactivation is performed by an audit manager (users.role = 'audit_manager'); actor holds the user's short_name.
- time_in_status: Time in a status pairs the transition that ENTERS it (to_status = X) with the one that LEAVES it (from_status = X) — two different invoice_history rows.
  invoice_history rows are transitions, not states. "How long from RECEIVED to READY" is the gap between the row entering RECEIVED (to_status = 'RECEIVED') and the row leaving it (from_status = 'RECEIVED' AND to_status = 'READY'), joined per invoice_id. Reading both timestamps from the single READY transition row (CASE branches over from_status/to_status inside a WHERE to_status = 'READY' scope) subtracts a timestamp from itself and yields exactly 0:00:00 — the play session's W3. Units: leaving.at - entering.at is an INTERVAL, not a number. Scale it only after EPOCH — AVG(EPOCH(lv.at - en.at)) / 3600.0 AS avg_hours — or count units with DATE_DIFF('hour', en.at, lv.at). AVG(lv.at - en.at) / 86400 AS avg_time_in_days (the post-coverage W3) divides an interval by a number and yields an interval of 0.041667 seconds, not 0.0417 days.
- rule_name_prefixes: findings.rule_name drops the code's rule_ prefix, and compliance findings are named compliance_<rule code> — a naming convention, never a join key.
  The rules engine's rule_rate_variance writes rule_name 'rate_variance', and so on. Compliance-intake findings arrive as compliance_CR-147 etc. — filtering rule_name LIKE 'compliance_%' selects exactly the compliance layer. But rule_name = 'compliance_' || rule_code is a DERIVED, NON-UNIQUE key (10 rule codes across 4,216 compliance_rules rows): used as a join condition it pairs every finding of a code with every rule of that code and fans out 17× and worse. Never join on it. For severity questions count compliance_rules directly — the invoices_to_compliance join path is the keyed road when invoice context is needed.
- rate_means_dollars_here: In review and contract context "rate" is a dollar unit rate (requested_rate, contract_rate, unit_rate), not a percentage.
  "What rate do auditors ask for", "the rate we requested", "the corrected rate" are dollars-per-unit questions answered from review_report_lines.requested_rate (see requested_rate_is_contract_rate) — never a share of findings. Percentage questions say "share", "how often", "what fraction", "what percent", and divide a count by its population; flag_rate, item_flag_rate and correction_application_rate are that kind. findings.category = 'CORRECTION' is the correction_ignored findings, and its share of all findings answers no rate question of either kind.
- corrections_never_resubmitted: A review that never drew a resubmission is neither applied nor ignored — leave it out of application rates and never count it as a rejection.
  109 reviews; 61 drew a resubmission (invoices.supplier_acceptance set on the reviewed invoice), 48 did not (supplier_acceptance NULL). Applied and ignored are judged only where a successor exists: 73 correction lines with a successor = 55 applied + 18 ignored, and the 18 are exactly the correction_ignored findings. Counting the 48 unanswered reviews as ignored, or reading review_reports.disposition (the auditor's verdict) as the supplier's response, overstates or inverts the answer. The per-line figure counts RATE and REMOVAL corrections alike; the rate-only subset (48 lines, 34 applied) is not the headline.

## Where to look
- Q: How many invoices received last week had findings?
  Join invoices to findings on invoice_id — an inner join: a LEFT JOIN counts every received invoice, not the flagged ones; COUNT(DISTINCT invoices.id); window on invoices.received_at anchored to the data's end (see data_coverage — "last week" means the final seven days ending 2026-05-30, i.e. received_at >= '2026-05-23 00:00:00' AND received_at < '2026-05-30 00:00:00').
- Q: Which supplier draws the most rate-variance findings?
  findings WHERE rule_name = 'rate_variance', joined through invoices to suppliers; GROUP BY suppliers.code ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC. Rate variance is the planted specialty of one supplier, so expect a dominant leader.
- Q: Is a given service item usually flagged for excessive hours?
  Use item_flag_rate with rule_name = 'service_hours_excessive' over invoice_lines filtered to the item_code — remember the composite line-level join (lines_to_findings).
- Q: Who closes the most reviews?
  auditor_throughput over invoice_history: to_status IN ('CLOSED', 'NO_REVIEW_NEEDED') GROUP BY actor, joined to users on short_name and filtered to role = 'auditor'.
- Q: How much recovery opportunity did each team close last month?
  recovered_opportunity per team/day (PRODUCTION_ROLLUP_SQL shape), windowed on invoice_history.at — anchored to the data's end, per data_coverage.
- Q: When auditors request corrections, what rate do they ask for?
  Dollars, not a percentage (rate_means_dollars_here): requested_rate_is_contract_rate — the answer is "the contract rate", shown as rate corrections at the contract rate beside the total, with the lowest and highest requested rates. Never the share of findings in category CORRECTION.
- Q: How often do suppliers actually apply the corrections we request?
  correction_application_rate (per correction, the default; name the reading). review_reports.disposition is the auditor's verdict on the invoice and says nothing about the supplier — APPROVED / all reviews is the wrong answer by two orders of magnitude.
- Q: Which supplier ignores our corrections the most, and how many?
  corrections_ignored_by_supplier — the correction_ignored findings, never a count of reviews or invoices without ACCEPTED (that counts reviews the supplier never answered).
- Q: List audit rejections by reviewer.
  corrections_ignored_by_auditor (ignored corrections per requesting auditor, the default; name the reading). REJECTED is not an invoice status: to_status never holds it, and review_reports.disposition holds only APPROVED / CORRECTIONS_REQUESTED. The reviewer is the actor who CLOSED the prior revision.
- Q: Show total invoiced amount per supplier, including suppliers with no invoice lines.
  LEFT JOIN from suppliers and SUM(invoices.invoice_total) with no COALESCE: suppliers with no invoices, and out-of-network suppliers whose invoices are born LAPSED with NULL totals and no lines, come back NULL — rendered as a dash, which is the truth ("nothing to sum"), where $0.00 asserts they invoiced nothing.
